reviewMethod: Read every current entry, all 280 stored occurrences and five claim anchors, with exact-turn actor state, ordinary-scene/Zen-bend prose, different-thing sense, counterexample, and reader-visible evidence controls. Karma-family entries were additionally tested against KARMA_DEBATE_BRIEF.md and KARMA_RESEARCH_BRIEF.md.
systemicFindings: The second sentence repeatedly assigns a whole deployment inventory to one actor or source, often making the actor grammatically become the object or image being defined.
Many explanations assert ordinary-scene details, contrasts, or Zen bends that no stored occurrence or claim anchor makes reader-visible.
Exact-turn review remains unreliable in named quotations, narrated sermons, anthology headings, and substring-contaminated hits; formal mechanical success does not cure those semantic defects.
The cohort therefore cannot be promoted from this exact hash set.

rows.finding: The prose names Sanyi Yu but the cited J37 occurrence belongs to 遠菴僼禪師; it also invents a moving-boat/fixed-notch proof absent from every stored quote.
Only 永覺元賢禪師's 西子 turn supports the copied-frown comparison; the prose assigns ridicule and borrowed-force claims to him across unrelated uses without exact anchors.
The stored idiom is 抱橋柱澡洗/洗腳, not holding the support instead of crossing. The explanation imports a crossing allegory and misnames 費隱禪師 as Feiyin Tongrong.
Two quotes explicitly begin 天童覺云 yet are labelled reviewed-unnamed. The prose then attributes a conceptual-measurement interpretation to Xutang without a stored predicate that establishes it.
The prose makes Yuansou Xingduan into what ties a donkey. It must distinguish the literal stake, doctrines or phrases called stakes, and the explicit 一句合頭語 tethering line by exact source.

The impaired-eye definition is plausible, but the stored evidence contains no diseased-eye self-definition under Yongming; the prose instead cites an unrelated J28 source and leaves the promised control invisible.

The first huge KWIC is 水月寺 substring contamination, not a moon reflection. Prose cites Hongzhi and X82 despite neither appearing in the selected evidence; the new reflection controls do not cure the contaminated row.
The stored X66 verse says 電光石火存機變 but does not establish the claimed deliberation-lag contrast or secure Baizhang as utterer; later speed uses need source-specific synthesis.

The explanation makes Furong Zixian the grammatical subject of the image and asserts residue-free melting without anchoring that inference; the selected Furong line instead contrasts gratitude and ingratitude.
It is Huizhong who requests a seamless monument from the emperor/patron, not 'Huangdi's demanded memorial.' The central case relation remains reversed.
The article makes Changqing Yingyuan into the instrument that is played or heard. Playing, blowing, singing, and hearing belong to distinct turns and must be mapped rather than collapsed.
Thirst and pursuit occur only in the narrated 渴鹿趂陽焰 row, not in the named Yongming/Yanshou source claimed by the prose. Attribute the ordinary scene to its actual evidence.
Baichi's stored line has the pearl rolling up waves; it does not place it under a dragon's jaw. The dangerous-depth and direct-attainment glosses are imported or assigned to the wrong clauses.
Dahui's 如優曇華時一現 supports rare appearance, but the entry generalizes encounters and arrivals without naming their actual witnesses and wrongly points to T51 rather than T47.
Konggu supports the failed-plucking paradox, but the article turns one line into a corpus-wide visible-versus-possessed theory without testing the paired 鏡花水月 and literary-preface uses.
The stored four lines praise or direct flowering; none supplies the claimed warning against lodging in deadness. The counterdeployment is asserted without evidence.
The stored rows show 隨色, showing, keeping, and questions, but not supply-according-to-demand. Liao'an is incorrectly made actor of the full deployment family.
Actor and instrument are conflated, and D48 mislabels a tomb inscription/title as utterer. The played/heard predicates need full-case attribution before semantic synthesis.

Three witnesses are recensions of the same Guizong question and one is an unnamed questioner; the entry overstates independent multi-source support and imports unobstructed inclusion not said in the stored lines.

The balance-pointer scene is useful, but the article assigns recognition, weighing, questioning, and judgment wholesale to Zishou; one 古尊宿 row also labels the questioner's context as the questioner despite 師云 owning the phrase.

The first occurrence attributes Nanquan's question to a record-title string labelled Huangbo. Travel cost is supported, but 'earned' and visiting-teacher accounting must be tied to the exact speaker and case.

The insult is attested, but the responsibility-for-monastery-food definition is not present in the selected rows; the prose assigns all eating, answering, and functioning claims to Cishou without exact evidence.
The rows attest an insult, but not the proposed stale-performance/living-force opposition. Several quoted Huangbo lines are assigned to later compilers or wrong section owners.
Bare-handed/open stealing is plausible, but praise, blame, and removal of another's footing are not established by the selected clauses and are all wrongly assigned to Quan'an Qiji.
The article makes Yibian actor of all daily-work uses. It must distinguish actual communal labor, quoted Pang material, and later questions about who performs the actions.
'Real heft' is an attractive interpretation rather than a stored claim. Questions, answers, and weight comparisons belong to different actors, not one Dongming deployment.
The burr's physical resistance is useful, but Yuanwu is made into the object 'given to bite.' Bite, swallow, and penetrate predicates must be attached to their actual speakers and uses.
The mat is correctly concrete, but all wearing, carrying, occupying, and hall uses are assigned to Zhihai Benyi. Source-specific institutional and encounter uses remain unsynthesized.
Sudhana's many visits are relevant, but one Shangu actor is made to cite, address, and judge every use. Figure, pilgrimage narration, direct address, and seekers compared with him need separation.
Presentation and sudden awakening are attested across rows, but Zihu is made actor of the whole story and the qualification-overturn inference is imported rather than stated by stored Zen speakers.

The ordinary-versus-special fare contrast is contradicted by the first line, which says 家常 tea and rice are insufficient without a special place. House custom, ordinary meal, and begging formula need honest separation.

Important controls were added, but the lead still claims Yongming's past-good/evil→present-pain/pleasure clause without storing it. The two 遮詮 anchors define the category but do not include 無因無果, the fox anchor is truncated before later ironization, and the non-karma senses remain 1/2/1-witness thin.

The J34 causal control is valuable, but '255 of 257 verified' is not proved by entry evidence and the opening overgeneralizes every use as fastening to a side, phrase, or position. Actor naming also misidentifies Mian Xianjie as source-work J34.

Condemnation is established, but Gu Xue Zhe, Gu Ting, and Juelang clauses remain marked compiler narration while prose attributes statements to them. The apophatic anchors define 遮詮 but do not show the promised 無因無果 formula.

The only witness says Gaofeng required finger/crown burning to show 誠重之心; it does not itself record anyone burning or identify a public vow. The article overstates event and institution from one source.

Literal finger burning is present, but vow-marking is only secure in one plea and the other rows are generic austerity/legal lists. The prose invents a unified enacted-vow role and leaves actors merely compiler-owned.
Three of four rows are false substring matches in 雖然頂上/躍然頂笠/自然頂門, not burning the crown. Only 然頂灼臂 supports the headword.
Three rows are false substring matches in 自然香/自然香潔. The remaining row means burn incense before an image, not burn incense on the body; the sense is unsupported.

The TOC row is not an utterance and explicit speakers are misassigned to section owners. Recipient and lineage-dedication claims are attested but must name each ceremony's actual actor and beneficiary.
The evidence shows institutional instructions and encounter answers, but not the claimed unified declaration of honor, gratitude, or commitment. Yunmen Lingkan cannot own all registers.
Several rows do name dedications, but Dongming's verse does not. The article assigns setting and beneficiaries wholesale to him and conflates documentary prayer with master speech.

The headword is a verb-object phrase 'light/burn incense' in some rows and part of the counting phrase 一炷香 in others; the single 'stick of incense' sense requires a grammatical split audit. Linji is wrongly made actor of all uses.

The corpus-wide term is improperly narrowed to Linji. Dedication, blessing, lineage debt, and time-measure uses require distinct exact sources and possibly different referents rather than one Linji-centered paragraph.

One row is a TOC, another is Pure-Land-oriented documentary prose, and the last occurrence's phrase sits in the master's sermon rather than an unnamed questioner turn. Vow maker and object are not reliably attributed.

The rows chiefly record four great vows and generic promise formulas; the article adds rescue, service, transmission, and future-act categories without mapping them, and it falsely attributes T2016 to Huineng.
The first row is compiler biography, not Xuefeng's utterance; none of the rows establishes public answerability as the defining feature. Oath content and actor must be read case by case.
The Fu Dashi and biography rows support establishing an oath, but the standing-obligation-versus-private-wish contrast is not in the evidence and no exact vow speaker is named.

The compact Huike case label is supported, but only one stored line criticizes imitation; the article assigns citation, compression, and criticism to Gulin and does not anchor the mind-demand and arm episode separately.

All rows merely quote the wall formula; none stores the promised 'going is also unmoving' control. The claim that wall-like means unshaken rather than physical facing is therefore not yet reader-visible evidence.

Five rows are the same question across recensions and the one answer is 邂逅到崖州, not an explanation of immovability. Muzhou is wrongly made questioner and all source independence/figure meaning is overstated.
